sentences.text: Revenue grew from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025, a 26.0% compound annual rate [F1][F10][F231].
Growth came in steps: 4.0% in FY2019 [D147], then 45.0% in FY2020 [D202] and 68.3% in FY2021 [D258].
Revenue rose 43.6% in FY2022 [D314], mostly from Embedded, which went from $246 million [S109] to $4.55 billion [S110] on the Xilinx acquisition [P41].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023 [D370], which the filing ties to a 25% drop in Client revenue [P35]; it then rose 34.3% in FY2025 [D483].
Client and Gaming contributed 19.0pp of FY2025's 34.3% revenue growth [D701][D483], Data Center 15.7pp [D694], and Embedded subtracted 0.4pp [D731].
Client revenue rose 50.8% [D755] to $10.6 billion [S124] on 31% more processor shipments and 15% higher average selling prices [P10].
Data Center revenue rose 32.2% [D693] to $16.6 billion [S98], driven by EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators [P13].
Operating-cost growth of 24.3% [D504] stayed below revenue growth of 34.3% [D483], giving an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% [D487], in line with net income growth of 164.2% [D485], as the diluted share count fell 0.1% [D506].
The 10.7% operating margin [F60] is above its 7.2% window median [D795] but ranks at the 17th percentile against semis peers, whose median is 31.0% [D818][D819].
Of the 3.3pp operating-margin gain in FY2025 [D499], 2.6pp sits in a residual [D516] the cited passages do not explain, while R&D added 1.7pp [D514].
Gross margin rose only 0.2pp to 49.5% [D498][F40] as product mix was partly offset by about $440 million of export-control inventory charges [P14].
Xilinx intangible amortization accounts for 3.3pp of the 16.8pp operating-margin fall in FY2022 [D343][D330][P46]; the cited passages do not explain the 8.5pp residual [D346].
Net margin of 12.5% [F80] sits 1.8pp above operating margin [F60] because the tax line was a benefit at a -2.5% rate [D469], including an $853 million release [P4].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $7.71 billion [F110] was 1.78x net income [D470], and free cash flow of $6.74 billion [F130] was 1.55x [D471], above the 1.17x window median [D810].
Capex of $974 million [F120] was 2.8% of revenue [D466] and 1.87x D&A [D472], up 53.1% [D490].
Working capital absorbed $2.4 billion in FY2025, mainly a $2.2 billion inventory build to support Data Center ramps [P3].
Operating cash flow includes $1.2 billion from the discontinued ZT Manufacturing business [P3], which the 1.78x ratio [D470] also reflects.
Net cash rose to $6.46 billion from $3.41 billion [D476][D419], even as total debt rose 138.0% to $4.10 billion [D508][D475].
Net cash is 18.6% of revenue [D477], the 100th percentile among semis peers [D826], against a peer median of -13.9% [D827].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion [X150] used 19.5% of free cash flow [D479] and left the diluted share count down 0.1% [D506].
The current ratio of 2.85x [F210] is the window high [D812], above the 2.19x window median [D813].
Inventory days rose each year from 106 [D312] to 165 [D481] (130 in FY2023 [D368], 160 in FY2024 [D424]), with the FY2025 build tied to Data Center ramps [P3].
Total debt rose 138.0% to $4.10 billion [D508][D475] in FY2025, and the cited filing text links only interest expense to the March 2025 notes [P6].
Net cash of $6.46 billion [D476] limits the debt risk for now, though both the debt step and the inventory build raise cash needs.
A roughly $440 million export-control charge on MI308 products hit FY2025 Data Center and gross margin results for one period [P12][P14].
Days inventory of 165 [D481] should fall back toward the FY2022 level of 106 [D312] in the FY2026 10-K; a further rise above 165 [D481] would reverse the cash-conversion read.
Free cash flow to net income of 1.55x [D471] should stay above the 1.17x window median [D810] in the FY2026 10-K; a drop below 1.17x [D810] would signal weaker conversion.
Operating margin of 10.7% [F60] should hold above the 7.2% window median [D795] in the FY2026 10-K; a fall below 7.2% [D795] would reverse the 3.3pp FY2025 gain [D499].
